findings.text: Upheld as a defect under Q9 and Q6. refuseLinksInside's `catch { return; }` swallows every readdirSync error. A .git, or a folder under it, that can be searched but not listed is skipped without a word, and git still writes through the links inside it. The neighbour readRegularFile refuses in the same case, so this is behaviour that disagrees with its neighbours, and a fallback that hides the cause. probes/security-round-five-findings.md F-1 (a) and (b) show the write going through. Fix: return only on ENOENT and refuse on any other error.

Advisory (Q10/Q2). commitChange's doc and CLAUDE.md call it the one place the failure rule lives, but adoptIn (store.ts:842-885) keeps its own frame with a different undo. The two copies agree on which error is thrown and on keeping the record, so this is prose overstating the code, not duplicated logic that disagrees.

Advisory (Q1). inEachRepo collects every result before the CLI prints. A fault that is not a refusal, raised in a later repository, means adopts already committed in earlier repositories are never reported. The doc does not say this.
Advisory (Q5). Refused collects the paths, but only its length is read. A count would do.
Advisory (Q10). refuseForeign's doc says 'holds a link', but the walk refuses any entry that is not a regular file or a folder.

Lowered to advisory. Against the base, this whole file is new in the diff. The removed 'null device' wording was an earlier draft of this same change and was never in the base, so the diff neither drops nor removes base prose under Q11. The comment as it stands cites git's documentation and states its scope (run on macOS, not on Windows).
Advisory, carried (Q5/Q8). readIntent is a one-line forwarder that only tests import.
Advisory, carried (Q5). keepBytes' default name and its return value are used only by tests.
Advisory, carried (Q2). adopt repeats underLeases' lease nesting. This is boilerplate-level duplication.
Advisory, carried (Q4/Q5). Three knobs are set only by tests: GitOptions.timeoutMs, resolveRepo's folderName and DoctorContext.gitVersion.
Advisory, carried (Q8). moduleVersion and readEntry are exports that only tests import. The rubric grades an unused export as advisory.
Advisory, carried (Q2). foldersByHand and projectFolders copy resolve.ts's folder listing.
Advisory, debt outside the change: `db as Db` casts a database that may be null. It is repeated at checks.ts:614.

Advisory (Q1/Q6). The 'a fault still does' half survives widening isRefusal to any KnowledgeError. One assertion, expect(stderr).not.toContain('knowledge/'), would kill that mutant. The reviewer graded it advisory: no criterion names the split.
Advisory. Only the line break is held; narrowing CONTROL to /\n/g leaves the suite green.
Advisory. No test holds the removal of the read cap (NO_CAP) on records and kept bytes. No criterion names it.
Advisory. No test holds underOwnLease's `started` rule.
Advisory. What the commands print for a listed folder with no repository is not tested.
Advisory (Q6). The links test does not prove 'before git runs': there is no stub git to show that no git call ran.
Advisory, carried. No test holds the order of record first, then kept bytes, in adoptIn.
Advisory, carried. A file added during a write's git calls is untested. This is a stated known limit.
Advisory, carried (Q5). The rebuild-order test depends on the internal renewal count.
Advisory, carried (AC-8). Only the version probe times out; the test does not check that the process is gone.
Advisory, carried (AC-2). The parent's .gitignore weakens the empty-status proof.
Advisory, carried (AC-13). Clipping is checked on the thrown message, not on the log line.
Advisory, carried (AC-2). The test resolves through the row, not through the manifest.

Upheld as a defect (personal-data). Who: the dropper. With what: a .git at mode 0300, or .git/logs at 0100, holding links. What they get: refuseLinksInside swallows the readdir error, and git writes the commit message into a file of the dropper's choosing (F-1 a), or appends a reflog line with the writer's name to it (F-1 b). This is personal data written outside the store. probes/security-round-five-findings.md shows both with git 2.54.0. Fix: fail closed on any error other than ENOENT.

Upheld as a defect (personal-data). Who: the dropper. With what: a link at <data dir>/knowledge/projects (or at knowledge/). What they get: ensureParents' recursive mkdir and createRepository follow the link. A project's whole repository, with the manifest, entries naming the writer and commits authored with the writer's name, is created in a folder outside the data directory. refuseForeign runs only on the repository's last component, never on its parents. probes/security-round-five-findings.md F-2 shows it ('folders made in the outside folder: 1', 'the entry there names the writer: true'). Fix: lstat-refuse a link at knowledge/ and knowledge/projects/ before listing or creating.

Advisory. Links inside the object folders are a read path into another repository, and a detached gc can be triggered. Nothing leaves the machine in part 1. Reasoned, not run. This is hardening to close before the sync.

Advisory. headOfGitDir follows a `ref:` out of .git; the probe shows it reads an outside file. The effect is availability and probing whether a file holds a hash; no personal data is written. This is hardening beyond the named areas.
Advisory. Dropped lock files and similar states fail as code git and stop the whole command. Availability only.
Advisory. With NO_CAP, a huge dropped record is read whole into memory. Availability only, and contained by the catch.
Advisory. Dropped file names are printed raw to the terminal. This is hardening outside the named risk areas.

Advisory. A person's own git with fsmonitor can leave a socket in .git, and the repository is then refused. The failure is visible at once (the error names the path and doctor warns), and no data is lost. The undo is manual and the ADR does not name the case.
Advisory. The cost of the walk is flat with history. The silent skip of an unreadable folder noted here is upheld as a defect under code-quality and security, not again here.
Advisory. Moving the commit into commitChange changes nothing for the existing writes. A failed alias commit still fails the write the person asked for.
Advisory. The revert report's 'not one this version of the store writes' also covers a corrupt record and a folder at the record's path, where it points at the wrong cause.
Advisory, carried. A locked lease or a timeout stops the later repositories, and a partial result exits 1 like a total failure.
Advisory, carried. 'was undone' also lists paths that were only unstaged, and at the extreme size the kept bytes may not be restored.

Advisory. The spec's risks section still says rebuild reads a corrupt repository's working tree; ADR 0024 records the newer behaviour. The rollback in spec.md:321 is stated and manual, which the rubric grades advisory, so this is not a missing rollback.
Advisory, carried. Leftover support folders from earlier builds of this branch stay in place, unread.
Advisory, carried and stated in Known limits. The module migration pass is not contained, and doctor does not warn when the module schema is behind.
Advisory, debt outside the change: lint processes 0 files in the worktree.
Advisory, debt outside the change: the p95 test is flaky.
Advisory, debt outside the change: the upgrade runner waits up to 10 s under BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
Advisory, carried. Function-level import cycles repo.ts<->resolve.ts and repo.ts<->author.ts. They are safe at runtime.
Advisory. The `invalid` code is documented as a repository refusal but is also raised for bad input. No inEachRepo caller reaches an input error today.
Advisory. The file map does not say where commitChange and inEachRepo live.
Advisory. 'a link anywhere inside its .git' claims more than the walk does; use the ADR's wording.
Advisory. The new sentence's placement makes the following sentence about erasure read as if it referred to refused repositories.
Advisory, carried. The spec's Design is not amended; ADR 0024 declares itself the later text and records each change.
Advisory, debt outside the change: SettingKey omits two keys.
Advisory, debt outside the change: no forward reference to ADR 0024.
Advisory, debt: the folder listing copy is already graded under code-quality.
Advisory (Q5/Q6). The refusal set has widened (sockets, FIFOs), and a refused repository's rows, the name among them, stay as last indexed. This is stated in ADR 0024:155, and nothing is lost.

Advisory, carried (Q1). The DELETE FROM meta cannot be undone, but its reason is stated at :17-18. It runs after the pre-upgrade backup. probes/withdrawn-module-meta-rows.md shows the keys have no other writer.
Advisory, carried (Q3). A file added during the write's git calls is counted but never read. This is a stated known limit.
Advisory, carried (Q6). The one-time VACUUM INTO backup under the write lock is not timed.
Advisory, carried (Q2). project_aliases is read by an unindexed project_id on a write path off the hook path. The table is small.
Advisory, debt outside the change: there is no index on project_aliases.project_id.
